name: tile-imageblock-lands-on-the-array-slice-the-argument-buffer-names
rationale: A tile kernel copies its imageblock to the array slice its argument buffer names, and leaves every other slice alone. `layered` is 1 and `sliceIdx` is 1, so the kernel takes `air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d_array` and addresses slice 1 of `colorTexArray`, a texture the argument buffer at binding 18 names at field offset 48. The output reads both slices: slice 0 must still hold its authored 0x5A and slice 1 must hold the tile, so a copy that ignored `sliceIdx` and landed on slice 0 fails on both halves. Each of the 256 texels carries a distinct dyadic rgb -- x/16, y/16, (16x+y)/256 -- exact at half width, so a transposed, shifted or partial copy moves bytes. Alpha is zero, below the `0x1C04` floor, and `resolveDepth` is zero, so the kernel neither tone-maps nor clears the cell: it copies the loaded render target through the imageblock untouched. That is deliberate. The tone-map arm calls `air.pow.v3f16`, a half transcendental Metal and MoltenVK are not required to agree on bit for bit, and it would make an exact comparison a test of the runtime's pow rather than of the imageblock copy. `colorBounds` spans the whole 16x16 tile so the region test admits the one thread, index 0 in the threadgroup, that performs the write.

name: dual-float4-zero-target-0
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns zero for both float4 color outputs; this case selects attachment 0 so each distinct sixteen-byte write is qualified independently while both poisoned attachments are bound in the same render pass.

name: dual-float4-zero-target-1
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns zero for both float4 color outputs; this case selects attachment 1 so each distinct sixteen-byte write is qualified independently while both poisoned attachments are bound in the same render pass.

name: eleven-bfloat-conversions-at-the-rounding-boundary
rationale: Eleven bf16 convert families the corpus calls but no case covered, over sixteen lanes of buffer-supplied operands the Metal compiler cannot fold. Twenty-four of the words sit where a one-step correctly-rounded integer-to-bf16 conversion and a two-step integer-to-f32-to-bf16 one disagree: bf16 keeps 8 significant bits and f32 keeps 24, so an integer just past a bf16 midpoint can round back ONTO that midpoint in f32 and then round away from it by ties-to-even. 33685505 is one such value (one-step 0x4C01, two-step 0x4C00) and 33947647 is one that diverges the other way (one-step 0x4C01, two-step 0x4C02), so a lowering cannot pass by biasing in a single direction. The remaining lanes are values both models agree on, including zero, one, the byte and half-word boundaries and the unsigned maxima. The bf16-to-integer slots pin truncation toward zero at every destination width from uchar to long. The 321st word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seventeen
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 17 and receives exact float4 zero from all sixteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A nineteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: linked-single-radix8-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-8 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: publish-a-timestamp-through-a-system-coherent-store
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.store.system_coherent.volatile.i32.p1i32 (4 case-less corpus sources). The MSL that spells it is not reachable from this SDK -- `coherent(...)` accepts only `device` and `threadgroup` here, and `coherent(device)` gives the device_coherent symbol -- so the host is the corpus's own `fence_update`, which is the whole point of the intrinsic in sixty lines: read a value out of a constant buffer and publish it to a device buffer another agent is spinning on, then fence. The published word is 0x5A3C7E11, which shares no byte with the 0xAB poison it overwrites and is asymmetric under every byte reversal, so a store that wrote the wrong width, the wrong endianness, or nothing at all is visible in the four bytes. The dispatch is a single thread because the intrinsic's argument is the whole buffer and a second thread would only repeat the same store.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position whose depth is explicitly set to zero. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached.

name: linked-single-offset-copy
rationale: One invocation selects the rank-one, one-element path. Zero enabled offset dimensions avoid indirect array access, zero strides address element zero in both direct buffers, and the linked secondary prefix is the exact retained zero-offset implementation. The kernel copies the authored 64-bit input into the poisoned output.

name: linked-single-lane-mx-dequantize
rationale: One invocation reads exactly four packed quantized bytes and one shared scale byte from the two authored device-array inputs. The exact linked primary float4 destination is the retained no-op callback; the sole poisoned destination element therefore remains byte-exact and proves the linked callback contract while the dequantization path executes.

name: precise-clamp-min-and-fmod-beside-two-fast-roots
rationale: Metal ground truth for fourteen uncovered families in one kernel: air.clamp.f32 (3 case-less corpus sources), air.clamp.u.v4i32 (3), air.clamp.s.v3i16 (3), air.fabs.f32 (3), air.min.u.v3i16 (3), air.fmod.f16 (3), air.fast_log.v2f32 (3), air.fast_rsqrt.v2f32 (3), air.fast_sinpi.f32 (3), air.fmod.f32 (1), air.fmod.v3f16 (1), air.min.s.v2i16 (1), air.min.s.v3i32 (1) and air.min.u.v3i32 (1) -- 32 sources. Under Metal's default fast math fabs, clamp and a float fmod compile to air.fast_*, which are already covered; the precise:: prefix is what reaches the plain symbols these sources call, and at half width there is no fast variant to avoid. Each clamp and min sees one operand below its bound, one inside and one above, with values past 2^31 on the unsigned lanes and negatives on the signed ones, so a lowering that dropped a bound, swapped the two or confused the two comparisons lands a different word. fmod is exact when its operands are, and fmod(-5.5, 4) is -1.5, which distinguishes it from a Euclidean remainder. fast_rsqrt is not correctly rounded on this host so it is asked only at powers of four, where its answer is a power of two; fast_sinpi returns a signed zero at integers so it is asked at 1.5, where the answer is exactly -1. fast_log is exactly zero at one, and its second lane is at ten, which separates a natural logarithm from a base-two or base-ten one and is checked against a float64 derivation to within one ULP.

name: set-counter-ceiling-division
rationale: A single loop-free invocation follows the nonzero-divisor branch with value ten and divisor three, then writes the exact ceiling quotient four through the argument-buffer device pointer.

name: set-counter-zero-divisor
rationale: A single loop-free invocation follows the zero-divisor branch with value seven and writes that exact value through the argument-buffer device pointer without division.

name: conv2d-a20-float8-unit
rationale: Structurally adapted one-invocation A20 convolution case with exact float postfix linkages and bounded declared resources.

name: zero-a-node-then-fill-six-of-its-sixteen-words
rationale:
Metal's software BVH node-zero encoder, 350 lines, one of two corpus hosts of `native/emitter/body/...::emit_raw_zero_memset` and the first authored case to reach it. The rule is the zero `llvm.memset` over a raw byte pointer: the kernel clears a 64-byte node at `innerNodeOffset` and then writes back only six floats and one word of it, so the sixty-four bytes test the memset and the seven stores together -- twenty-eight of the cleared bytes must still be zero afterwards and would not be if the memset were short, misaligned, or skipped.

One thread. The 256-byte constant template is memcpy'd over the destination header first, so the case also pins that copy; its first word is 0x210, whose bit 4 selects the refit path and whose bits 8..14 give the loop two iterations, and whose bit 0 clear selects `primitiveCount` rather than zero and `instanceCount` zero rather than the count. `refitDataOffset` is 512 and `innerNodeOffset` 576, so the three written regions -- header, refit pair, node -- are disjoint and the 640-byte selected region holds two untouched gaps that must still be the authored 0xAB. `primitiveMotion` is false, so the keyframe count is the literal 1 rather than the template's 4242, which is left in place as a decoy. The six bounding-box floats are 1 through 6 and a seventh, 999.0, sits in the four bytes the kernel skips between them, so a contiguous six-float copy would be caught. Nothing is computed in floating point -- the floats are loaded and stored unchanged -- so the answer is exact and association-proof.

`authored_bounded`: the only loop runs `(templateWord >> 8) & 127` times, which the authored constant fixes at 2. Every argument AIR marks unused is bound with 0x99 filler, including both argument buffers and their eight nested pointers.

name: clear-first-vfx-curve-info-word-1
rationale: Two loop-free invocations exercise both sides of the thread_position_in_grid.x equality branch: index zero atomically clears the first word of the 20-byte curve record, while index one leaves every remaining poisoned byte untouched.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-three-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 and 3 and receives exact float4 zero from both linked _uber_clear bodies. A five-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected as the result. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel for byte-exact comparison.

name: linked-single-radix8-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-8 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: hand-each-quad-lane-its-own-channel-and-hand-the-answers-back
rationale: median_rgb_filter_local_histogram_one_channel_per_thread gives each quad one destination column and each of the quad's first three lanes one colour channel, and it moves colour between those lanes with nothing but quad broadcasts: lane 0 alone samples the source, air.quad_broadcast.v3f32 with lane 0 hands that rgb to lanes 1 and 2, each lane bins its own channel, and then air.quad_broadcast.f32 with lanes 1 and 2 hands the green and blue bins back to lane 0, which is the only lane that writes. Both symbols are therefore load bearing in a way the destination shows: without the v3f32 broadcast lanes 1 and 2 bin an undefined colour, and without the two f32 broadcasts every destination texel would be grey. The three channels differ in every one of the 32 visited texels, so a broadcast off by one lane is visible at all of them. The case collapses the median to the identity rather than deriving a window: the filter radius is 0, so the histogram takes one sample, and the rank is 1, so the search stops on the first bin, which is that sample's. What survives is exactly the shader's quantisation -- clamp to [0, 1], times 255, truncate to a ushort, back to float times the float nearest 1/255 -- and the eight column colours are multiples of 1/16 offset per row by multiples of 1/32, so every product with 255 lands at least a quarter away from an integer and the truncation has no boundary to sit on. One column's red is 1.5 and another's green is -1/4, so both arms of air.fast_clamp.f32 are taken. The alpha lane bypasses the histogram, so it reports the sampled texel unquantised and each of the 32 is distinct. Both origins are non-zero and different from each other -- the source is read from (1, 2) and the result written at (2, 1) -- so the 64 destination texels the kernel does not touch keep their initial bytes and pin the write rectangle. num_pixels_in_y is 1, which is what makes the kernel's second row loop unreachable.

name: horizontal-mask-dilation-across-a-four-texel-reach
rationale: A 14x1 ushort mask with one marker exactly four texels from one candidate and five from the other, so the inclusive window bound decides which of the two is dilated and every value stays an exact small integer.
